b7-001.reason: Thanks for Whewell's marriage gift and mentions beginning Hermann und Dorothea - direct reply to the gift paragraph.

b7-002.reason: Catherine's paragraph reports on the state of the correspondence; Darwin's reply acknowledges the whole string of letters received.

b7-003.reason: Formal testimonial to George Gray's courtesy, exactly answering Children's official inquiry.

b7-004.reason: Reply para 3 is the wrap-up answering Kemp's deference paras 2 and 6 (both excluded) and dangles on 'what I have said' - the advice in para 2, which is not in the answer.

b7-005.reason: Postscript on 'the late discussions on the rotatory action of whirlwinds' answers Redfield's whirlwind/vortex paragraphs.

b7-006.reason: Darwin rebuts 'the good people of Shropshire, who say I shall find cruizing in the South-seas stupid work' - verbatim from the paired paragraph.

b7-007.reason: Directly answers the Langtons' departure for Madeira/West Indies with messages for Charlotte.

b7-008.reason: Reply paras 6-7 are the 'great question of houses' - Regents Park, Tavistock Square, furnishing - answering Emma's house and kettles paragraphs.

b7-009.reason: Answers the Macaw Cottage news, Gordon Square comparison, Margaret the maid, and the plea to rest; sheets sentence is only a stray reference.

b7-010.reason: 'You will not think of reading the Elements' answers Emma's stated intention to try Lyell's last book.

b7-011.reason: 'Respect at the pleasant tone of your last letter' answers Kemp's gracious, uncomplaining paragraphs.

b7-012.reason: Acknowledges the series of letters and 'my Father likes my Journal' - both raised in the paired paragraph about the parcel and the Journal read aloud to Papa.

b7-013.reason: Reply para 3 answers Fox's 'last letter' (incoming paras 5-6): Ryde, the domestic menagerie and actually collecting beetles appear only there, and para 3 of the question says the opposite ('Not one capture have I made').

b7-014.reason: Reply para 6 forwards the enclosed note to Dr Richardson exactly as asked; para 1 is the general acknowledgment plus Darwin's own business, not a response to another paragraph.

b7-015.reason: Reply para 4 is the sentimentality/Lyell paragraph answering Emma's paras 1 and 4 (scolding and Lyell's book), both excluded from the question.

b7-016.reason: 'I think myself of sufficient consequence for you to care to hear our plans' directly echoes Emma's postscript, and the ring/plans paragraph answers her opening.

b7-017.reason: 'I have advised you to the best of my judgment' and the papers-safe offer answer Kemp's deference on publication and his thanks for the trouble taken.

b7-018.reason: Answer text (Kemp's seeds, papers safe, advice) appears nowhere in this reply letter to Catherine Darwin - it comes from a different correspondence entirely.

b7-019.reason: 'Go & get the Respirator for Uncle Jos' plus the sign-off answers the respirator request and the goodbyes.

b7-020.reason: Picks up Herbert's 'heaps of parchment' lawyer joke and overrating of Darwin's natural history, plus the shared Barmouth memories.

b7-021.reason: Answers the Clift/Megatherium bones, the carriage-expense query and the father's kindness about money, all raised in the paired paragraphs.

b7-022.reason: 'I told you I should write to you as if you really were my own dear wife' answers Emma's scolding that no trifle is too small, and the Lyell visit answers her Lyell's-book paragraph.

b7-023.reason: Thanks Whitley for the kind letter, regrets they will not meet, and promises to write - answering his request to meet and correspond.

b7-024.reason: Explicitly answers Caroline's puzzle about what is new in Herschel's Old Testament chronology.

b7-025.reason: 'Your account of Erasmus' visit to Cambridge has made me long to be back there' - Whewell and Sedgwick named as in the question.

b7-026.reason: Answers both halves of Henslow's paragraph: the Atriplex identification and the profitable tumulus/urn exhibition.

b7-027.reason: Point-by-point reply to Lyell: the invitation, the Journal, De Beaumont, 'begin to hope', coral theory, and the date of the Coral Reefs book.

b7-028.reason: The Charlotte/Rio paragraph is not in this reply to Susan at all; it belongs to a different letter.

b7-029.reason: Pots and pans, the 'poor dear old lady, you ought to have thought of this before' retort, Tavistock Square's price and the servant/housekeeper all come straight from the paired paragraphs.

b7-030.reason: Reply para 1 is a complete paragraph on Robert Mackintosh's newspaper affair and Lord Palmerston, answering Emma's para 3, which is excluded from the question.

b7-031.reason: Answers Henslow's offer of the Beagle place point by point and returns the condolence for Ramsay.

b7-032.reason: Answers the billing mistake, the consignment directions and the brother's address, plus expedition news.

b7-033.reason: The whole reply works through Kemp's paper: seed layer height above the river, boulders and glaciers, the runner/climbing plant, and the 'too bold' damp-climate speculation.

b7-034.reason: Thanks for the meteorological pamphlets and the geological reports that Redfield says he will forward.

b7-035.reason: 'You ask me about the specimens which I send to Cambridge' answers Catherine's question about the quantity of stones sent there.

b7-036.reason: Answers both the Whig/Tory politics and Herbert's ill health attributed to want of exercise.

b7-037.reason: 'You enquired in yr. last letter about Lyell's Speech' plus the leaving-Cambridge news answer the paired paragraphs; the Missionary paper is a parenthetical aside.

b7-038.reason: Covers the letters and the hoped-for niece (para 1), Erasmus turned householder (para 5) and the horrifying 'little books with extracts' (para 3).

b7-039.reason: Short acknowledgment that the letter reached him off the Galapagos; same exchange, no dangling reference to an excluded paragraph.

b7-040.reason: 'Who would not be proud to receive such a nice affectionate one?' answers Emma's affectionate scolding opening; the Tollet and writing-time asides are passing references.

b7-041.reason: Reports progress on the Glen Roy paper and states when her last letter arrived - both explicitly asked for in the paired paragraph.

b7-042.reason: The Whigs/Colonial Slavery/exercise paragraph is from the Herbert correspondence, not from this formal reply to the Treasury.

b7-043.reason: Formal reply acknowledging the 1000 pounds grant and submitting the publication plan the Treasury asked for.

b7-044.reason: The 'your house / our house' scolding quotes Emma's opening paragraph; the calligraphy jibe is a passing aside within an otherwise responsive paragraph.

b7-045.reason: 'I am indeed very sorry to hear of poor Col. Leighton's death' answers the paragraph reporting it.

b7-046.reason: Babington's Atriplex verdict and 'I would as soon believe myself capable of playing a hoax on the public as I would believe you to be so' answer Kemp's soil-contamination defence directly.

b7-047.reason: Closing salutation and the fungi postscript from the same reply to Whitley; the letter has only these two incoming paragraphs, so nothing excluded is being answered.

b7-048.reason: 'I hope & trust Charlotte will be enthusiastic about Tropical scenery... whether she has actually gone to Rio' answers the Charlotte-to-Rio news in para 2.

b7-049.reason: Acknowledges the letters and responds to the Sedgwick praise quoted in para 1, closing with the farewell that answers para 5.
